hattusa.name: Hattusa
hattusa.slogan: A Bronze Age capital still guarded by stone lions.
hattusa.line: About 30,000 clay tablets recovered here form the main corpus of Hittite literature.

amasyatombs.name: Pontic King Tombs
amasyatombs.slogan: Kings carved their final rooms into the cliff above the river.
amasyatombs.line: Strabo, born in Amasya, wrote that these rock tombs belonged to the kings of Pontus.

yaliboyu.name: Yalıboyu Houses
yaliboyu.slogan: Timber mansions leaning over the Yeşilırmak at golden hour.
yaliboyu.line: Young Ottoman princes were sent to Amasya to govern; Murad II and Selim I were born here.

yazilikaya.name: Yazılıkaya
yazilikaya.slogan: Hittite gods march in stone through an open-air rock sanctuary.
yazilikaya.line: Chamber A's rock relief shows 64 deities in procession, mostly carved in the late 13th century BCE.

harsenakalesi.name: Harşena Castle
harsenakalesi.slogan: A ruined citadel on the rock that watches over Amasya.
harsenakalesi.line: The fortress above the town was already described by Strabo around 2,000 years ago.
